newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity continues rise to new highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity continues rise to new highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures continued their uptrend reaching new contract highs Friday on strength from the physical power market in the U.S. West, industry sources said.

Continued triple-digit temperatures in the interior of the Southwest region have been pushing spot power prices higher, and futures have been following to new lofty levels through much of this week, the sources said.
"The loads are strong in the West, and this market just keeps going higher," said one power futures trader.

As of 1250 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) NYMEX futures were up $1.49 at a new contract high of $25.75 following trade as low as $25.00, while July PV was up $1.30 at a new contract high of $27.50 after trading as low as $27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
August and September PV were also strong, reaching new contract highs.
June California Oregon Border (COB) was up $1.47 at new contract high of $19.65 after trade as low as $18.60, while July was up $1.00 at a new contract high of $20.20 per MWh.
Heat in the Southwest was said to be spurring power demand along with some Western power supply constraints, industry sources said.

Short-term Western power prices were said to be rising again Friday, with peak PV power for Monday delivery pegged at near $46.50 per MWh from a range of $39.00-$43.00 on Thursday for Friday delivery.

The interior section of the Southwest was expected to experience triple-digit readings through the weekend, while the California coast would continue to enjoy temperatures in the 70s-80s degrees Fahrenheit.
In the Northwest, major cities like Portland and Seattle are expected to see cloudy skies and temperatures in the 60s-70s.

Availability of spot power supply across the West remained tight due to ongoing plant outages and reduced generation at several Northwest hydropower dams due to new flood-control restrictions on discharge.
The 400 MW Bonanza coal-fired station in Utah is set to shut Friday for a two-week maintenance outage.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in Arizona was heard to shut late today for about two weeks of planned maintenance.
The Platte River Power Authority's 262 MW Rawhide coal-fired plant in northern Colorado was expected to shut over the weekend for a brief maintenance outage.

Also, southbound power transmissions on the 2,990 MW DC (direct current) segment of the Pacific Intertie will be cut by around 1,000 MW over the weekend for maintenance work, according to the Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) schedule.
BPA, which operates the Northwest portion of the interstate transmission system, said the work would be carried out between 1600 PT on Saturday through 1700 PT on Sunday.
As of 1250 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas was trading up three cents at $2.225 per million British thermal units.
COB open interest for May 15 rose 272 to 5,912, while PV open interest rose 200 to 6,720, NYMEX said.
